textHi:
Directions. Identify the segment of the sentence which contains the grammatical error. If there is no error mark 'No error' as your answer.

explanationEn:
The correct answer is Option 3 i.e., 'we will have had'- the error lies in this part only.

  • This is a conditional sentence, and in this type of sentence, one sentence depends upon the other because of cause and effect.
  • In this case, this type of sentence follows a special structure.
  • Conditional words are If, until, unless, as soon as, when, while, as long as, since, etc.
  1. Conditional word + subject + v1/v5 + object, subject + will/ shall/ may + v1 + object.
  2. If + subject + v2 + object, subject + would/ should/ could/ might + v1 + object.
  3. If + subject + had + v3 + object, subject + would/ should/ could/ might + have + v3 + object.
  4. Had + subject + v3 + object, subject + would + have + v3 + object.
  • The given sentence follows rule number '4', and according to the rule, the error lies in Part 'C'.

For example- Had John learned driving, he would have landed a job as a trainer in the driving school.

  • In the given sentence, 'will' is wrongly used instead of 'would' before 'have' in the main clause.

Hence, 'will have had' should be replaced by 'would have had'.

So, the correct sentence is:

"Had M.S. Dhoni led us in the T20 World Cup Championship 2019, we would have had two World Cups with us today."

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Wednesday announced its decision to make interoperability mandatory for all full-KYC prepaid payment instruments (PPIs) and other payment infrastructure. The regulator simultaneously announced an increase in the permitted outstanding balance in PPIs to Rs 2 lakh from Rs. 1 lakh and allowed cash withdrawals from full-KYC non-bank wallets. The regulations effectively bring wallets at par with bank accounts in terms of service offerings.
RBI governor Shaktikanta Das expressed displeasure with the lack of effort on the part of industry players to voluntarily move towards interoperability. The central bank had issued guidelines in October 2018 for adoption of interoperability on a voluntary basis for full-KYC PPIs. As the migration towards interoperability has not been significant, Das said, it will now be mandatory for full-KYC PPIs and for all payment acceptance infrastructures. At present, cash withdrawal is allowed only for full-KYC PPIs issued by banks. The allowing of cash withdrawals from all PPIs, in conjunction with the mandate for interoperability, will boost migration to full-KYC PPIs and would also complement the acceptance infrastructure in Tier-III to -VI centres, the RBI said. In addition, the RBI-operated centralised payment systems (CPSs) – RTGS and NEFT — will be opened up to non-bank payment system operators like PPI issuers, card networks, white label ATM operators and trade receivables discounting system (TReDS) platforms. The measure is aimed at minimising settlement risk.
Responding to a query about data breaches at non-bank PPIs and the role of the RBI's supervisory architecture thereof, executive director T Rabi Sankar said the regulator's objective would always be to protect the customer and make transactions as safe as possible. "To that extent, like we have issued to banks recently, we are looking at issuing guidelines that could lay down the basic minimum norms for cybersecurity and other security issues. As far as instances of such issues are concerned, we are seized of those matters and we are taking all the steps required to reduce the possibility of such events," he said. Manoj Chopra, VP & head – products and innovation, InfrasoftTech, said interoperability might help wallets claw back the space they had lost to banks and other players with the rise of Unified Payments Interface (UPI) and the new KYC requirements. "Cashbacks offered also did not help much. Interoperability will provide that much needed push for wallets and PPI providers," Chopra said, adding that the transition would be fraught with risks. Customers will have to be more careful about digital frauds and wallet providers will have to beef up their technology infrastructure to be able to manage these risks.
As wallets become enabled with most transaction features available on bank accounts, they will be able to effectively compete for micro-savings from the under-banked segments, said Ketan Doshi, MD, PayPoint India.

textEn: Ratio of age of Rita and Sita is 5 : 7. After 4 years sum of ages of them is 68. Mita is 4 years younger than Sita. Find the Mita's present age?
textHi: रीता और सीता की आयु का अनुपात 5 : 7 है। 4 वर्ष बाद उनकी आयु का योग 68 है। मीता, सीता से 4 वर्ष छोटी है। मीता की वर्तमान आयु ज्ञात कीजिए।
explanationEn:
Given:

Rita : Sita = 5 : 7

After 4 years, (Rita + Sita) = 68

Mita is 4 years younger than Sita

Formula used:

Let Rita = 5k, Sita = 7k ⇒ Sum = 12k

Future sum after 4 years each: (Rita + 4) + (Sita + 4) = (Rita + Sita) + 8

Calculations:

⇒ (Rita + Sita) + 8 = 68

⇒ Rita + Sita = 60

⇒ 12k = 60

⇒ k = 60 ÷ 12 = 5

⇒ Sita = 7k = 7 × 5 = 35

⇒ Mita = Sita − 4 = 35 − 4 = 31

∴ Mita's present age = 31 years.

दिया गया है:

रीता : सीता = 5 : 7

4 वर्ष बाद, (रीता + सीता) = 68

प्रयुक्त सूत्र:

⇒ मीता = सीता − 4 = 35 − 4 = 31

∴ मीता की वर्तमान आयु = 31 वर्ष।

textEn: By selling 45 lemons for ₹40, a man loses 20%. How many should he sell for ₹24 to gain 20% in the transaction?
textHi: 45 नींबू को ₹40 में बेचने पर, एक आदमी को 20% की हानि होती है। लेनदेन में 20% का लाभ प्राप्त करने के लिए उसे ₹24 में कितने बेचने चाहिए?
optionsEn: None of the above/More than one of the above
optionsHi: उपर्युक्त में से कोई नहीं/उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
explanationEn:
Given:

By selling 45 lemons for ₹40, a man loses 20%.

Calculation:

Selling price of 45 lemons = 40

Loss % = 20%

Cost price of 45 lemons = (40/80) × 100 = 50

Cost price of 1 lemon = 50/45 = Rs. 10/9

If a man sells a lemons for Rs. 24 and gains 20%, then

Cost price = (24/120) × 100 = Rs. 20

If cost price of 1 lemon is Rs. 10/9 then number of lemons which can be brought in Rs. 20 = 20 × (9/10) = 18 lemons

Hence, option 2 is correct.

Alternate Method

Let's first find the cost price (CP) of the 45 lemons.

If selling price (SP) = ₹40 represents 80% (100% - 20% loss), then:

80% of CP = ₹40

=> CP = ₹40 × 100/80

=> CP = ₹50

Now, the cost price of 45 lemons is ₹50.

Cost price of 1 lemon = ₹50/45

Cost price of 1 lemon = ₹10/9

Now,
Selling price (SP) = 120/100 × CP of 1 lemon

SP = 120/100 × (₹10/9)

SP = ₹12/9

SP = ₹4/3

Now,

Number of lemons = Total amount / Selling price per lemon

Number of lemons = ₹24 / (₹4/3)

Number of lemons = ₹24 × 3/₹4

Number of lemons = 18.
explanationHi:
दिया गया है:

45 नींबू को ₹40 में बेचने पर एक व्यक्ति को 20% की हानि होती है।

गणना:

45 नींबू का विक्रय मूल्य = 40

हानि% = 20%

45 नींबू का क्रय मूल्य = (40/80) × 100 = 50

1 नींबू का क्रय मूल्य = 50/45 = 10/9 रुपये

यदि कोई व्यक्ति नींबू को 24 रुपये पर बेचता है और 20% का लाभ होता है, तो

क्रय मूल्य = (24/120) × 100 = 20 रुपये

यदि 1 नींबू का क्रय मूल्य 10/9 रुपये है, तो नींबू की संख्या जो 20 रुपये में लायी जा सकती है = 20 × (9/10) = 18 नींबू

अत:, विकल्प 2 सही है।

textEn: A 300 meters long train passes 450 meters long platform in 30 seconds. In how much time the train will pass a 700-meter long bridge?
textHi: एक 300 मीटर लंबी ट्रेन 450 मीटर लंबे प्लेटफॉर्म को 30 सेकंड में पार करती है। ट्रेन 700 मीटर लंबे पुल को कितने समय में पार करेगी?
explanationEn:
Given:

The length of the train is 300 meters.

The train can pass 450 meters long platforms in 30 seconds.

Formula used:

The speed of the train = {(the length of the train + the length of the platform or bridge or another train)/time}

Distance = Time × Speed

Calculation:

The speed of the train = {(300 + 450)/30} m/s

⇒ The speed of the train = {750/30} m/s

⇒ The speed of the train = 25 m/s

Now, to cross the 700-meter long bridge the train has to be travelled (700 + 300) meters = 1000 meters

So, required time = 1000/25 sec = 40 sec

∴ The train will pass the 700 meters long bridge in 40 seconds.
explanationHi:
दिया गया है:

ट्रेन की लंबाई 300 मीटर है।

ट्रेन 450 मीटर लंबे प्लेटफॉर्म को 30 सेकेंड में पार कर सकती है।

ट्रेन की गति = {(ट्रेन की लंबाई + प्लेटफॉर्म या पुल या किसी अन्य ट्रेन की लंबाई)/समय}

दूरी = समय × गति

गणना -

ट्रेन की गति = {(300 + 450)/30} मीटर/सेकंड

⇒ ट्रेन की गति = {750/30} मीटर/सेकंड

ट्रेन की गति = 25 मीटर/सेकंड

इसलिए, अभीष्ट समय = 1000/25 सेकंड = 40 सेकंड

∴ ट्रेन 700 मीटर लंबे पुल को 40 सेकेंड में पार करेगी।

__ < __ < Purple < __ < __ < __

  • Case 2: Blue < Yellow < Purple < Red < Green < Black
